newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Banespa seen in cenbank hands by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Banespa seen in cenbank hands by year-end.

text.p: The transfer of Sao Paulo state bank Banespa to the Central Bank as part of a $36 billion debt renegotiation deal should take place before the end of the year, Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola said.
Brazil's Senate was expected to vote on Thursday on debt restructuring agreements between the federal government and nine states, including Sao Paulo, Loyola said.
Approval of the Sao Paulo deal by the upper house would leave a favorable vote in the Sao Paulo state legislature as the last remaining hurdle, Loyola said.
"The transfer of Banespa could be carried out by the end of the month," the Central Bank president said.

Under the terms of a recently signed deal for the renegotiation of Sao Paulo's debt, Banespa would be placed under Central Bank control and prepared for privatization by private administrators. Sao Paulo owes about $20 billion of its total $36 billion debt to Banespa.
Loyola said he expected the Central Bank to take over several other state banks as state governments take advantage of the debt renegotiation terms it is offering.

Nine state governments have signed preliminary agreements to privatize assets and take other cost-cutting measures in return for longer debt repayment terms from Brasilia, and several others are negotiating similar deals.
